Other Advance Degree in any of the following: Divinity, Theology, Mission Integration, Ministry, Spiritual Care, PastoralCounseling, Bioethics. Two or more years of Clinical Experience providing Spiritual/Pastoral Care or Counseling in a clinical setting, upon hire
Experience working in a clinical setting,addressing pastoral, spiritual and ethicalissues, as evidence by 4 units of ClinicalPastoral Education (CPE) from an ACPE accredited site

Provides pastoral support and counseling to patients/residents, families, personnel and medical staff, taking special note of patients newly admitted, critically ill, dying and those preparing for surgery. Measurements: Observation, Feedback.

Assesses pastoral / sacramental needs of patients, families and personnel and provides follow-up as needed. Makes referrals for sacramental ministry of Catholic patients for Catholic chaplains or Eucharistic ministers. Measurements: Observation, Feedback.
Provides prayer and worship opportunities for patients, hospital personnel, medical staff and local church and civic community. Measurements: Observation.

Responds in an appropriate and timely manner to all referrals for chaplain services and provides documentation in both the patient's medical record and departmental records, including assessment, intervention, pastoral plan and evaluation. Measurements: Observation, Documentation, Feedback.

Collaborates with members of the interdisciplinary team and medical staff to provide total patient care. Participates in patient care conferences on assigned clinical units as well as other interdisciplinary hospital meetings. Measurements: Observation, Minutes of Minutes, Patient Care Documentation.

Provides effective pastoral intervention during Code Blue/Code Pink/Code Yellow and other patient crisis. Acts as liaison between family, hospital personnel and medical staff. Measurements: Observation, Feedback, Patient Care Documentation.
